title: Indian Polity Test 1 (Constitution & Institutions — most probable)

questions.q: The Constitution of India was adopted by the Constituent Assembly on:
questions.explain: Adopted on 26 Nov 1949 (now Constitution Day); it came into force on 26 January 1950.

questions.q: The Constitution of India came into force on:
questions.explain: India became a Republic on 26 January 1950, the date chosen to honour Purna Swaraj Day of 1930.

questions.q: The Chairman of the Drafting Committee of the Constitution was:
questions.explain: Ambedkar chaired the Drafting Committee; Rajendra Prasad was President of the Constituent Assembly.

questions.q: The President of the Constituent Assembly was:
questions.explain: Rajendra Prasad presided over the Constituent Assembly and later became India's first President.

questions.q: Originally, the Constitution of India contained:
questions.explain: Amendments have since expanded it to about 470 Articles, 25 Parts and 12 Schedules.

questions.q: At present, the Constitution of India has how many Schedules?
questions.explain: Originally 8 schedules; four more were added by amendments (9th land reforms, 10th anti-defection, 11th Panchayats, 12th Municipalities).

questions.q: The words 'Socialist' and 'Secular' were added to the Preamble by the:
questions.explain: The 42nd Amendment (mini-Constitution) also added 'Integrity' and the Fundamental Duties.

questions.q: The idea of Directive Principles of State Policy was borrowed from the Constitution of:
questions.explain: DPSPs came from Ireland; Fundamental Rights came from the United States of America (USA) and the parliamentary system from Britain.

questions.q: The Fundamental Rights in the Indian Constitution were borrowed from:
questions.explain: The United States of America (USA) also inspired judicial review and an independent judiciary.

questions.q: The federal system with a strong Centre was borrowed mainly from:
questions.explain: Canada's model of federation with a powerful central government suited India's unity needs.

questions.q: The Concurrent List in the Seventh Schedule was borrowed from:
questions.explain: Subjects in the Concurrent List can be legislated by both the Centre and the States.

questions.q: The Fundamental Duties were borrowed from the Constitution of:
questions.explain: Added later by the 42nd Amendment, 1976, on the Swaran Singh Committee's recommendation.

questions.q: Article 14 of the Constitution guarantees:
questions.explain: Article 14 gives equality before law to every person in India.

questions.q: Article 21 protects:
options: Protection of life and personal liberty
questions.explain: Article 21 is the most widely expanded right; the Supreme Court has read many rights (privacy, clean environment) into it.

questions.q: Free and compulsory education to children aged 6-14 years is guaranteed by:
questions.explain: Article 21A was inserted by the 86th Amendment, 2002; the Right to Education (RTE) Act followed in 2009.

questions.q: Dr Ambedkar described which Article as the 'heart and soul' of the Constitution?
questions.explain: Article 32 lets citizens move the Supreme Court directly for enforcement of Fundamental Rights through writs.

questions.q: The writ 'Habeas Corpus' is issued to:
options: Command a public officer to do his duty
Stop a lower court from exceeding its powers
Produce a person before the court (against illegal detention)
Question a person's title to a public office
questions.explain: Habeas Corpus = 'to have the body' — it protects personal liberty; Mandamus = command to do duty, Quo Warranto = question title to office.

questions.q: The office of the President of India is mentioned in Article:
questions.explain: Article 52 says 'There shall be a President of India'; impeachment is in Article 61.

questions.q: The minimum age required to become the President of India is:
questions.explain: President and Vice-President need 35 years; Rajya Sabha 30; Lok Sabha 25.

questions.q: The oath of office to the President of India is administered by the:
questions.explain: The Chief Justice of India (CJI) (or the senior-most Supreme Court judge available) swears in the President.

questions.q: The Vice-President of India is the ex-officio Chairman of the:
options: National Institution for Transforming India (NITI) Aayog
questions.explain: The Vice-President presides over the Rajya Sabha; the Lok Sabha elects its own Speaker.

questions.q: The Council of Ministers is collectively responsible to the:
questions.explain: Under Article 75, the ministry stays in office only while it holds the confidence of the Lok Sabha.

questions.q: A Money Bill can be introduced only in the:
questions.explain: Under Article 110, a Money Bill originates only in the Lok Sabha; Rajya Sabha can only recommend changes within 14 days.

questions.q: Who certifies whether a Bill is a Money Bill or not?
options: The Speaker of the Lok Sabha
questions.explain: The Speaker's decision on a Money Bill is final.

questions.q: The Supreme Court of India was established under Article:
questions.explain: Article 124 establishes the Supreme Court; High Courts are under Article 214.

questions.q: The Comptroller and Auditor General (Comptroller and Auditor General of India (CAG)) of India is appointed under Article:
questions.explain: The Comptroller and Auditor General of India (CAG) audits the accounts of the Union and the States; Article 76 = Attorney General, 280 = Finance Commission, 324 = Election Commission.

questions.q: The Election Commission of India functions under Article:
questions.explain: Article 324 gives the Election Commission the power to conduct elections to Parliament, State Legislatures and the offices of President and Vice-President.

questions.q: The Union Public Service Commission (UPSC) is provided for in Article:
questions.explain: Article 315 creates the Union Public Service Commission (UPSC) for the Union and State PSCs for the states.

questions.q: The Finance Commission, constituted every five years, is set up under Article:
questions.explain: The Finance Commission recommends how taxes are shared between the Centre and the States.

questions.q: The first law officer of the Government of India is the:
options: Comptroller and Auditor General of India (CAG)
questions.explain: The Attorney General advises the Union Government on legal matters and can speak in Parliament (without voting).

questions.q: The 42nd Amendment of 1976 is popularly known as the:
questions.explain: It made sweeping changes — Preamble, Fundamental Duties, DPSPs and more — hence 'mini-Constitution'.

questions.q: The Right to Property was removed from the Fundamental Rights by the:
questions.explain: Property is now only a legal/constitutional right under Article 300A — no longer a Fundamental Right.

questions.q: The power of Parliament to amend the Constitution is given in Article:
questions.explain: Article 368 lays down the amendment procedure; the Supreme Court's Kesavananda ruling limits it by the 'basic structure' doctrine.

questions.q: A joint sitting of both Houses of Parliament is provided for in Article:
questions.explain: The President summons a joint sitting (presided over by the Lok Sabha Speaker) to resolve a deadlock on an ordinary bill.

questions.q: The Rajya Sabha is:
options: A permanent body, never fully dissolved
questions.explain: One-third of Rajya Sabha members retire every two years; each member's term is 6 years.

questions.q: The normal term of the Lok Sabha is:
questions.explain: Unless dissolved earlier, the Lok Sabha continues for five years from its first meeting.

questions.q: The President can issue an Ordinance when Parliament is not in session under Article:
questions.explain: Article 123 empowers presidential ordinances (213 is the Governor's corresponding power); an ordinance must be approved within six weeks of Parliament reassembling.

questions.q: The Governor of a State is appointed by the:
questions.explain: The Governor holds office during the pleasure of the President.

questions.q: Impeachment of the President of India can be initiated in:
questions.explain: Under Article 61, the charge can be preferred by either House and investigated by the other.

questions.q: The maximum strength of the Rajya Sabha, as fixed by the Constitution, is:
questions.explain: The Rajya Sabha can have at most 250 members (238 elected + 12 nominated); its present strength is 245.
